corrections.brick_solid: The Layer 0 row gives k = 0.17 W/mK and cp = 330 to 440 J/kgK at 1980 kg/m3. Both fail a physical plausibility check: fired clay brick at that density conducts near 0.9 W/mK and stores near 800 J/kgK. This is the baseline wall, so an implausibly low conductivity would make current construction look insulated and shrink every reported difference. ASHRAE values substituted; confirm with Layer 0.

costs: Indicative delivered cost, not a measured property and not supplied by Layer 0. The Layer 0 material source file states these must be replaced with locally sourced values. Treat every rupee figure derived from them as provisional.
absorptances: Layer 0 supplied no thermal, solar or visible absorptances. Every material carries the schema defaults of 0.9 thermal and 0.7 solar. Surface colour changes solar gain on an exposed wall by a large fraction, so a painted absorber or a whitewashed roof needs its own measured value before it is reported.
ground_temperature_source: Undisturbed earth temperature at 0.5 m from the EPW GROUND TEMPERATURES header, calculated from this weather file
ground_temperature_note: NASA POWER TSOIL1 for 2015 to 2024 is also in the Layer 0 delivery and gives -8.9, -8.5, -7.4, -2.4, 2.8, 7.7, 12.3, 11.9, 7.2, 0.5, -4.4, -8.8 C. It was not used because it is a MERRA-2 reanalysis cell whose grid elevation is 4533 m against the 3256 m of the site, so it does not describe this ground. The EPW header values are derived from the same weather year the simulation runs on, so they stay consistent with it.
